correctness.rationale: Perfectness makes the target basis squares independent, so every isomorphism is monomial. A monomial M acts by A ↦ M A (M^(2))^(-1), with entrywise squaring multiplicative on monomial matrices. Every nonidentity diagonal tuple forces one distinct entry per column to vanish. If k points move, k(2n−k) ordered matrix positions move; each nontrivial coordinate orbit gives at most one free entry. Conditioning on invertibility costs at most γ_q^(-1); summing fixed-point probabilities gives the expectation bound. Burnside identifies the relative error with E(S−1), and each orbit contributes the same total stabilizer mass, giving the separately claimed class-uniform bound by s≤2(s−1) on s≥2. For k≤n/2 the rank-loss exponent is at least 3kn/4, and above n/2 it is at least 3n²/8, proving the stated fixed-field error. An independent n=2, q=3 replay at /workspace/branches/33f8145a-9743-4cd5-8fc3-e91fcc439adc/check_record4_small.py gives 48 invertible matrices, stabilizer frequencies 40 and 8 for orders 1 and 2, and 7 classes, 2 nonrigid. The uploaded verifier was inspected but not run; the finite check is not the general proof.

originality.rationale: The exact indexed comparison is stronger than a shared first-order count. The distinct October 25 corank-enumeration record proves a bound for the sum of nonidentity monomial fixed-point fractions on all matrices for this same fixed-field action. Restricting its numerator to GL and dividing by the GL density gives the mean-extra-stabilizer bound and rigidity; Burnside then gives both sampling versions. Its Eq. (7) already gives the very same support-k rank loss used here, and Eq. (9) gives an explicit diagonal bound of smaller asymptotic order than this record's diagonal term. The particular simple diagonal estimate and packaging as η do not provide a substantively distinct bound. The later November 2 entry also gives sharp asymptotic equivalents in exactly this regime. This is a statement-level overlap decision, not a claim to establish historical priority from catalogue timestamps.
residual_risks: The review does not settle priority among public entries or identify every earlier binary asymptotic. The decisive fixed-field overlap is independent of binary chronology.
